hyps.why: With edge 2->3 removed, node 2 has no route to the output, so changing edge 0->2 has essentially no effect instead of its usual positive gain.
Node 2 is dead when edge 5 is none, so adding a conv on edge 1->2 cannot help.
If edge 0->1 is none, node 1 is identically zero, so a conv on 1->3 contributes nothing.
With node 1 receiving no input, the 1->2 conv only processes zeros and gives no gain.
When the 2->3 path is cut, the direct 0->3 edge carries most of the computation, so making it a conv matters much more.
A residual skip helps when a deep conv path exists, but adds little when the cell lacks such a path.
Upgrading an existing 1x1 conv to 3x3 yields a much smaller gain than replacing none, pooling, or skip.
Replacing the strongest op on the main output edge with parameter-free pooling causes the largest accuracy drop.
With 0->3 already removed, cutting 1->3 leaves only one path to the output and hurts much more than when a direct path exists.
Zeroing node 1 wastes the 3x3 conv on edge 1->3, so removing edge 0 is more harmful when that conv is present.
